//: Composite indexes for every production query that needs one.
Firestore creates single-field indexes automatically, so a query filtering or
ordering on ONE field needs nothing here. A composite index is required the
moment a query combines an equality filter with an orderBy on a different
field, or combines two equality filters.
Every entry below was derived by reading the queries in backend/repo/ rather
than by waiting for production to raise FAILED_PRECONDITION. The source query
is named against each one so that deleting a query and leaving its index, or
adding a query and forgetting its index, is visible in review.
IMPORTANT, AND NOT YET DISCHARGED: the Firestore emulator does NOT enforce
composite index requirements. It answers any query, indexed or not. That means
the local test suite cannot prove this file is complete or correct — a missing
entry here passes every test and then fails on the first real request against
a real project. These must be deployed to the staging project and the suite
re-run against it before launch. See docs/PRE_LAUNCH_REPORT.md, which records
this as an outstanding blocker rather than a passing check.

indexes.//: repo/orders.js listOrders() — status filter with the stable seq ordering.
repo/orders.js ordersForPhone() — the customer detail page.
repo/orders.js ordersForProfile() — a signed-in customer's own history.
customerAuth.js claimProfile() — unclaimed guest orders for a proved address.
repo/orders.js orderStats() — refundDueValue: cancelled AND already paid.

//: The order document carries its lines and its status history as arrays of
objects. Firestore indexes every field of every array element by default,
which for a 60-line order is 60 index entries per indexed subfield, written
on every order and paid for on every order. Nothing queries by line
contents — the items are read as part of the order and never filtered on —
so those indexes are pure cost.
Exempting them is the single largest write-cost saving available in this
schema. It is listed under fieldOverrides rather than left to the default
because the default is expensive and silent.

fieldOverrides.//: Delivery areas on the settings document. Never queried.
